info.bio:
Passengers, fue el proyecto paralelo de la banda irlandesa U2, dirigida por el productor musical Brian Eno en 1995, quienes participaron en el disco 'Original Soundtracks 1'. El concepto del disco es presentar canciones de las bandas sonoras de películas imaginarias. El único single de este álbum es la canción 'Miss Sarajevo'. Los integrantes de Passengers fueron:

    * Brian Eno
    * Bono
    * Adam Clayton
    * The Edge
    * Larry Mullen

podcast.title: Brian Eno's Pseudonymous Liner Notes
podcast.body: For the Passengers album, Original Soundtracks 1, producer Brian Eno contributed liner notes under two different fake names: Ben O'Rion and CS Both-Fop. The liner notes were filled with various in-jokes and hidden references, adding to the mystique of U2's pseudonymous project. "Who was this Ben O'Rion and CS both-fop who wrote the liner notes? Well both were fake names given to Brian Eno, and the deeper you go into the liner notes, the more in jokes you'll find."

xref.title: Final Flight Details (October 20, 1977)
xref.body: The Convair took off from Greenville at 5:02 PM Eastern Time on October 20, 1977, with 22 passengers, Captain McCurray, and First Officer Gray. They climbed to a cruising altitude of 12,000 feet for the approximately three-hour flight to Baton Rouge, initially carrying 5.5 hours' worth of fuel. "The Convair took off from Greenville at 502 Eastern Time, with 22 passengers and Captain McCurry and first officer Gray at the controls."

xref.title: Pilot's License and Plane Crash (2005, 2008)
xref.body: Ed Robertson obtained his pilot's license in 2005 and was featured in the TV show "Ed's Up," documenting his journey to secure a float plane license. On August 24, 2008, his Cessna 206 amphibious plane lost speed and crashed into a grove of trees about 300 meters from shore on Baptiste Lake near Bancroft, Ontario. Ed and his three passengers miraculously walked away unharmed. A Transportation Safety Board investigation could not find a concrete cause, ruling out pilot error, mechanical malfunction, or weather, suggesting an air current anomaly as the likely reason for the loss of lift and airspeed. "Ed and his three passengers were all able to walk away. The transportation safety board launched an investigation but couldn't find a concrete cause."

xref.title: Cessna 206 Crash (2008)
xref.body: Ed Robertson, who obtained his pilot's license in 2005 and was featured in the TV show "Ed's Up" while working on a floatplane license, was involved in a plane crash on August 24, 2008. At around 12:30 pm, his Cessna 206 amphibious plane lost speed after taking off from Baptiste Lake near Bancroft, Ontario, and crashed into a grove of trees about 300 meters from shore. Despite the crash, Ed and his three passengers were all able to walk away. "On the afternoon of August 24, 2008, Ed took off an Ascena 206, one of these amphibious planes, from Baptiste Lake near Bankroft, Ontario."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Identification Challenges
xref.body: Identifying the victims was complicated because many passengers had been playing poker before the crash, and their wallets, which were kept nearby, were scattered everywhere into the swamp. "Identifying everyone was difficult because remember, at the time of the crash, many of the passengers were playing poker. They'd had their wallets up and they'd been scattered everywhere into the swamp."

xref.title: In-flight Activities and Ronnie Van Zant's Sleep
xref.body: During the flight, some passengers played poker, while others drank and partied, celebrating that it would be their last flight on the old Convair. Ronnie Van Zant, exhausted from the previous night, was curled up with a pillow on the floor near the front of the cabin, trying to sleep after taking sleeping pills to block out the noise. "Ronnie was curled up with a pillow on the floor towards the front of the cabin, trying to get some sleep."

xref.title: Jean Odom's Outburst
xref.body: Amidst the unfolding disaster, security chief Jean Odom was remembered by some as yelling, "I hope you two sons of bitches lived through this so I can kill you both," directed at the pilots, reflecting the sheer terror and anger among the passengers. "Some people remember security chief Jean Odom yelling, I hope you two sons of bitches lived through this so I can kill you both."

xref.title: Music Videos and Self-Promotion
xref.body: Despite her day job, she never abandoned her musical aspirations. She began recording songs and producing music videos, which she distributed to her limo passengers on VHS tapes. "She started recording songs and making music videos, which she put on VHS tapes that were handed out to her limo passengers."

xref.body: While Noel Gallagher was stuck in the Severant Tunnel and continuously strumming the opening chords of what would become "Acquiesce," a fellow passenger eventually screamed, "The Amine mate. We've heard enough of the guitar now." "something that eventually prompted one of the passengers to scream, the Amine mate. We've heard enough of the guitar now."

xref.title: Pilots' Announcement and Crash Preparation
xref.body: With both engines dead, the plane rapidly descended from 4,500 feet, leaving only the sound of wind over the fuselage. Captain McCurray informed the passengers, "We're out of gas," instructing them to adopt the crash position by putting their heads between their legs and buckling up tightly. "McCurry turned to his passengers. We're out of gas, he said. Put your head between your legs, in the crash position, and buckle up tight."
